s1.syndrome_frame: A congenital, exophytic, smooth, and soft lesion on the tongue
salient_findings: 1.5-cm diameter lesion on the midline of the dorsal tongue
Lesion has been present since birth
Partly fatty, submucosal lesion with mild contrast enhancement
key_facts: 20-year-old man with no significant medical history
1.5-cm diameter, exophytic, smooth, regular, and soft lesion on the midline of the dorsal tongue
Lesion has been present since birth
Lesion has not changed in size or character
Vital signs are within normal limits
MRI showed a 1.5-cm protuberant mass arising from the dorsal aspect of the tongue
Lesion appears partly fatty, likely submucosal
Lesion demonstrates mild contrast enhancement
Intact overlying mucosa
No involvement of intrinsic tongue muscles
Sublingual space and major salivary glands appear normal

shortlist.label: Lingual Thyroglossal Duct Cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Congenital origin and midline location of the lesion

shortlist.label: Dermoid Cyst of the Tongue
shortlist.why_kept: Congenital, exophytic, and smooth characteristics of the lesion

shortlist.label: Lipoma of the Tongue
shortlist.why_kept: Partly fatty appearance on MRI and submucosal location

shortlist.label: Congenital Granular Cell Tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Congenital origin and potential for mild contrast enhancement

shortlist.label: Choristoma of the Tongue
shortlist.why_kept: Congenital, exophytic, and smooth characteristics of the lesion with potential for varied tissue types

raw.rationale: The lesion's midline location, presence since birth, and partly fatty appearance on MRI are consistent with a Lingual Thyroglossal Duct Cyst, which is a congenital anomaly that can present as a smooth, regular, and soft mass in the midline of the tongue.

rejected.label: Dermoid Cyst of the Tongue
rejected.why: While dermoid cysts can be congenital and present in the tongue, they are less likely to be partly fatty and in the midline compared to Lingual Thyroglossal Duct Cysts.

rejected.label: Lipoma of the Tongue
rejected.why: Lipomas are typically found in older adults and are not usually present at birth, making this option less likely.

rejected.label: Congenital Granular Cell Tumor
rejected.why: These tumors are rare and not typically described as partly fatty or having the same characteristic midline location as Lingual Thyroglossal Duct Cysts.

rejected.label: Choristoma of the Tongue
rejected.why: Choristomas are rare benign tumors composed of normal tissue in an abnormal location, but the description provided does not strongly support this diagnosis over Lingual Thyroglossal Duct Cyst.
